author: Zara Barker
title: Larry texted 'I'm not right,' and 'I'm about to lose it,' hours before Maya was last seen alive - NewsBreak
text:
By Zara Barker ,
5 hours ago
CHULA VISTA, Calif. (FOX 5/KUSI) — “I’m not right,” and “I’m about to lose it” Larry Millete texted those messages to his boss around noon on Jan. 7, 2021, the day Maya was last seen alive.
Larry’s phone records are in the spotlight on day 10 of this trial.
On Jan. 8, 2021, Larry’s phone records show that he called his Aunt Kathy at 6:35 a.m. That phone call lasted 51 seconds, and then the phone lost cell connection for 12 hours.
The phone then reactivated the cell connection at 6:33 p.m., near his home.
Larry’s phone records on Jan. 8, 2021: 6:35 a.m. — Larry called his Aunt Kathy for 51 seconds 6:35 a.m. — Larry’s phone turns off cell service for 12 hours 6:33 p.m. — Larry’s cell service re-activated, received a call from his father Villaver testified there weren’t any transactions with cell site locations, and no data for about 12 hours. Villaver said the data doesn’t show why or how the phone lost connection, but said it could have been because the phone was powered off, or that the battery or the cell phone was destroyed.
On Jan. 8, 2021, Larry received multiple calls, but because there wasn’t any cell connection, the calls went to voicemail. He received calls from his mom, his dad, his aunt, his boss, and then later in the evening, from Maya’s brother.
Cell phone data Peter Villaver, a crime analysis administrator with the San Diego County District Attorney’s Office, testified that Maya’s cell phone terminated cell service at 1:25 a.m. on Jan. 8, 2021, in the San Miguel Ranch area of Chula Vista.
Villaver, who began testifying on Tuesday afternoon and finished his testimony on Wednesday, said he can’t determine why the phone stopped pinging to cell service, but it could have been because the phone died, was turned off or was put into airplane mode.
Maya’s phone has never been found.
Defense cross-examining Villaver Defense Attorney Colby Ryan questioned Villaver for most of the afternoon. Villaver testified that his report’s conclusion said the last known location of Maya’s phone was consistent with being in the San Miguel Ranch neighborhood, within the same location of her home. But Ryan pushed back and said it was “more likely than not,” alluding to the fact that they cannot say with 100% certainty. Villaver agreed that the cell data points are estimated.
Ryan questioned Villaver regarding his qualifications to perform tests to determine where Maya’s phone may have been. Ryan also questioned him on if he had the proper paperwork for the cell phone records.
Ryan claimed that Villaver’s three-day test, which he conducted to show where Maya’s phone may have pinged, may have been different when Maya had been using their phone because of potential construction zones or different foliage, since it was a different season.
He claimed Villaver didn’t note in his initial report any construction happening in Chula Vista during the time of the cell phone records obtained.
Maya’s sister-in-law on the stand Genesis Nicolas-Tabalanza, Maya’s sister-in-law, was on the stand Wednesday afternoon. She said that Maya moved in with her, her husband and their two kids in their two-bedroom apartment for a short period of time in the summer of 2020. She said Maya told her that she needed space from Larry to clear her head.
Genesis said that during the time Maya was staying there, Maya would wake up in the morning, drive a 4-Runner from the apartment to her home, switch cars to her Lexus SUV, go to work and then drive home to switch cars before she went to the apartment again. Genesis said she did this because Larry allegedly told her that he didn’t want Maya to park the Lexus on the street near their apartment.
During that time Maya was there, Genesis testified that Larry texted her often and asked about Maya, asked where she was going if she left the house, and would say, “Can you check if she’s wearing her ring?”
“He wants to save his marriage,” Genesis said. She said that Larry wanted to know where Maya was, her whereabouts, and what to do so that Maya would not separate from him. Genesis said that during this time, she talked to Maya about the marital issues, but not as often as Larry shared.
Text messages between Genesis and Larry On April 3, 2020, Larry texted Genesis: “Hey Gen what’s that plant you mentioned before? Hemlock?”
Genesis : “Why r u asking that question? Im beginning to worry about you”
Larry : “Just curious”
“Tired”
Genesis : “Oh do not give up”
Larry: “Thanks Gen”
“I admire you”
“Your strength”
Genesis: “I ask God daily for strength. You need to truly surrender your burdens to him. This is a difficult journey.”
Larry: “What’s the plaint again”
“Your right I pray for strength daily”
“I slip up with surrendering my anxiety and burdens. That’s where I’m lacking.”
April 21, 2020, text messages: Larry: “Hi Gen were you with Maya at 1530″
Genesis: “ Yes. We walked like 5 times at the track”
Larry: “Ty”
Genesis: “I try to get in touch with her when I go to the office. We chat and walk.” “She looks happy.”
Larry: “TY”
Genesis testified that Larry would often text her and ask about Maya
April 29, 2020, text messages: Larry: “Hey Gen are you still will Maya”
“With”
“Please don’t tell her I’m asking”
Genesis: “No, I left because they are going upstairs so Robyn can hi to the rest of the policy team.”
Larry: “Was it just you and Tobin in her office?”
Genesis: …..(unknown message here)
Larry: “Thanks. Still a bit insecure and paranoid”
Genesis said it made her feel uncomfortable because she felt like she needed to report to Larry where Maya was. Genesis said that during this time, she had just learned about their marriage problems.
May 8, 2020 , text messages : Larry: “Please help me with Maya.”
Genesis: “What’s goin on? Is she at work?”
Larry: “Yes”
“We had a rough morning and shes said shes done and wants out. Our marriage is on its last leg. I’m scared she’s going to actually going to leave this time.”
“When tones get tough she threatens to leave”
“Times”
May 15, 2020 , text messages : Larry to Genesis : “Did she spend the night there? Or leave during the night? I have knots in my stomach for some reason.”
“Panic or anxiety attack”
“Sorry to bother you.”
May 17-18, 2020, text messages: 9:11 a.m. Larry to Genesis: “Good morning Gen are you with Maya”
May 23, 2020, text messages: Larry to Genesis: “Where’s Maya”
That same day, Genesis to Larry: “I see May as done…”
“That’s just an opinion”
Judge grows visibly frustrated Wednesday morning began with about a 40-minute discussion between the attorneys and Judge Enrique Camarena, continuing the conversation from Tuesday regarding the defense wanting to try to impeach police detective Jesse Vicente’s investigation in the case because they believe the investigators did not properly investigate anyone else, and only investigated Larry Millete.
The defense is trying to cast doubt in the jury’s mind and show that they believe Maya’s affair partner, Jamey Laird, was not properly investigated.
They claim that he lied during multiple police interviews, and despite being the one who talked to Maya the most, he didn’t reach out to Maya after she went missing.
The judge and both attorneys were visibly frustrated as the judge ruled the defense’s line of questioning could not cross the boundary of trying to point the finger at anyone else, which would go against the judge’s ruling of not allowing third-party culpability in this case.
The judge said Laird’s involvement did not pass the four-part test that would allow third-party culpability.
“In the pretrial motion, Judge Camerana specifically ruled that the defense could not point the finger at Jaime Laird, and in making that ruling, he looked to the California Supreme Court case of People v. Hall, which set forth a specific test which must be met,” true crime writer and Attorney Aleida K. Wahn said. “It’s four essential elements that must be met in order to use third-party culpability as a defense, and in this case, Judge Camernena did not find that that test was met.”
Wahn has been following this case since the beginning and has been in the courtroom during the trial.
The conversation ended on Wednesday morning so the day’s proceedings could begin, but this is likely not the last time this conversation will be brought up.
